title: Fourier coefficients of the odd slice
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the sign cube of dimension $n+1$, and let $S$ be a subset of the first $n$ coordinate indices. Take half the difference between the slices of $f$ obtained by fixing its first coordinate to $1$ and $-1$. The Fourier coefficient of this function at $S$ equals the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at the frequency consisting of the first coordinate together with the indices of $S$ shifted up by one.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the sign cube of dimension $n+1$
